title: Assignment 2.1: School composition and school choice
text:
Among regular Dutch primary schools, is the neighbourhood composition of four-year-old intake associated with that of pupils already enrolled in the previous year, after accounting for where families live?
Level: inference. If families respond to a school’s existing composition, a small change in intake could persist. We ask whether the data are consistent with that possibility. They cannot by themselves show that composition causes school choice.

title: Assignment 2.1: School composition and school choice
text:
Datasets
We use four public datasets:

DUO pupil origins (2022–2023): counts by school location and home postcode (PC4). We use these to calculate each school’s neighbourhood composition.
DUO school totals (2022–2023): total enrolment per school location. We use these as the denominator for coverage.
CBS postcode population (2022): residents by migration background and PC4. We use these to describe the neighbourhoods linked to pupils’ postcodes.
DUO pupils by age and postcode (2023): counts by age, school, and home postcode. We inspect age-four cells as a possible intake measure and quantify suppression.

title: Assignment 2.1: School composition and school choice
text:
Exploratory process

Data and cleaning
The download script caches the source files. Functions in R/ then prepare, inspect, and plot the data.


Code
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(scales)

source("scripts/download.R")
source("R/prepare.R")
source("R/plots.R")

data <- prepare_data(paths)
intake <- check_intake(paths[["intake"]])
schools_2023 <- filter(data$schools, year == 2023)
selected <- filter(schools_2023, eligible)
#' Format counts with thousands separators.
format_n <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)


Each row in the DUO origins data represents one school–postcode–year; each plotted point represents one school. We keep school codes as text, retain regular primary schools in 2022 and 2023, and join CBS to pupils’ home PC4.
The neighbourhood composition proxy is the pupil-weighted average of the share of residents in CBS’s historical “non-western migration background” category. Both enrolment years use the 2022 CBS release.
DUO marks suppressed counts as -1, we treat them as missing. A postcode enters the weighted average only when its count is exact and CBS reports at least 50 residents. A school is eligible when at least 50 pupils are matched and coverage is at least 80%.


Code
plot_coverage(data$schools)









Of 6,150 regular primary school locations in 2023, 3 lack a usable total and 5,656 pass both quality rules. Overall median coverage is 94.4%. Coverage combines count suppression, unusable postcodes, and missing CBS values.


First patterns


Code
plot_composition(data$schools)









The middle half of included schools spans 4.0% to 16.3%. This variation makes the question worth investigating, but may reflect residential segregation and geography as well as school choice.


Code
ggplotly(plot_persistence(data$pairs), tooltip = "text")






Among 5,536 schools meeting the rules in both years, the median absolute change is 0.07 percentage points. The 7 orange triangles flag changes larger than five points for closer inspection. Large changes could also arise from mergers or changing data coverage.


Next stage
We also checked DUO’s October 2023 file by age and home postcode. Among 28,607 school–postcode cells with at least one four-year-old, 69.9% are suppressed as <5. Age four is a proxy for intake. Small flows will therefore need a defensible treatment before modelling.

Keep neighbourhood composition as a labelled proxy.
Examine four-year-old intake separately from existing pupils. Most pupils remain enrolled between years, so persistence in total enrolment is expected.
Check school continuity and coverage before interpreting large changes.
For the later inference, account for home-postcode and school differences and existing recruitment links. Show estimated associations with uncertainty; these exploratory plots do not answer the causal question.



Sources and reproducibility
DUO pupil origins, DUO school totals, DUO pupils by age and postcode, and CBS table 83503NED. The first knit downloads these public sources; later knits reuse local copies. The raw data is not committed. Source releases may be revised. Code: thatmariia/bdst_dv.
